subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards keep full-content CardKit updates with a different throttling strategy, add an opt-in append/delta mode, or steer slow tenants to non-streaming delivery?
rationale: The available evidence shows a real latency regression, but the latest live comment challenges the open coalescing PR and an append mode would add config surface while departing from the official CardKit full-text contract.

options.title: Require Feishu Strategy Decision
options.body: Pick the permanent payload mode policy after redacted live Feishu/Lark timing, request-count, and final-content proof compares full-content coalescing, append/delta, and non-streaming fallback.

options.title: Keep Full-Content Default Only
options.body: Continue treating CardKit full-content updates as the only supported streaming mode and ask the open PR or a follow-up to prove a stronger cadence fix.

options.title: Add Opt-In Append Mode
options.body: Allow affected deployments to choose append/delta payloads, accepting the compatibility and documentation burden because some tenants appear too slow with full accumulated content.

recommendation.title: Require Feishu Strategy Decision
recommendation.body: Pick the permanent payload mode policy after redacted live Feishu/Lark timing, request-count, and final-content proof compares full-content coalescing, append/delta, and non-streaming fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata identifies this handle as the Feishu community maintainer, and the decision is specific to Feishu/Lark channel behavior.
